steps.text: A sundial tells time using the Sun's shadow. Let's see how it works.
Move the Sun across the sky and watch the shadow of the pointer move.
As the Sun moves from east to west through the day, the shadow swings around — and its position shows the time.
In the morning the shadow points one way, at noon it's shortest, and by evening it points the other way. That's how a sundial marks the hours.

coach.mission: Use the Sun's shadow to read time on a sundial.
whenStuck: Move the Sun and watch how the shadow shifts.
Notice where the shadow falls at morning, noon, and evening.
whenWrong: The shadow moves as the Sun moves — its position tells the time.
At noon the Sun is highest, so the shadow is shortest.
whenCorrect: Right — the shadow's position marks the time of day.
Good — the shadow is shortest at noon.
coach.done: You've seen how a sundial tells time by shadow. Explore more, or move on when you're ready.
